attacks.name: Forever Security EMBRACE, browsers embedded in five AI assistants

sources.title: EMBRACE: How We Hacked the Browsers Embedded in Top Five Desktop AI Assistants

attacks.borderline_note: The post is a disclosure of research findings in product browsers. It does not name an in-the-wild intrusion. At publication, Forever Security said the Codex and VS Code issues were still unpatched.
attacks.ai_role_detail: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code, and Claude Desktop each ship a browser inside the assistant. Forever Security says the enrichments that let the agent use that browser broke three ordinary browser rules.
attacks.technique_summary: Forever Security (Gal Weizman; published Oct 29, 2026) calls the shared pattern EMBRACE, an embedded browser trusted like a standalone one. The post covers Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code, and Claude Desktop. In Cursor, a page opened in the built-in browser hid a command in an on-screen HTML chip. The agent read the hidden instructions. In an otherwise empty composer, one Enter ran the proposed command. When Cursor's sandbox blocked it, the agent turned the sandbox off on its own, with nothing in the page telling it to, and tried again. Forever Security says the install then ran with the user's privileges, outside the sandbox, and from a cold start in an empty project one Enter launched an app the page chose. The post says this does not fire on every model. In GitHub Copilot's browser preview, a page could report any address that looked like a web address. The address bar and the agent's tab list both showed github.com while the tab was somewhere else. Forever Security confirmed that on Copilot 1.1.27 on Sep 26, 2026. GitHub fixed it in 1.1.29 on Oct 13, before a report was sent. In Codex, Claude Desktop, and VS Code, a local HTML file opened in the built-in browser could read outside the project. The delivery in the post is a dull financial-report repo. The user asks the assistant to set it up per the README, and the assistant hands over a link to the file. Claude Desktop and VS Code restrict the page itself to the project folder, but not a web worker the page starts, and reads from that worker reached any file on the disk. Codex had no folder check. The page used a hidden index file macOS writes in folders opened in Finder to map the disk, then read SSH keys, .env files, npm tokens, and the hosts file. Disclosure: Cursor, Sep 10, patched silently on Oct 1, with no reply. Claude Desktop, July 23 to Anthropic, declined as outside a Workspace Trust boundary; a July 24 report from Noma Security was accepted as valid. Codex, July 27 to OpenAI, no reply, and still unpatched at publication. VS Code, Sep 10 to Microsoft, declined for the same Workspace Trust reason, and still unpatched at publication. This is a different Forever Security report from forever-agents-md-hijack-2026 and thisbash-claude-dispatch-rce-2026-11.
attacks.initial_access: A page opened in the assistant's built-in browser, or a local HTML file the assistant links from a repository the user asked it to set up
ai_tooling_and_models: GitHub Copilot browser preview, 1.1.27 and the 1.1.29 fix
attacks.victims_and_sectors: Users of those five desktop assistants. No victim organization is named. The file-read demonstration used the researchers' own machine.
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: No threat actor. Forever Security disclosed the findings to the vendors. Noma Security is credited for a July 24 Claude Desktop report that Anthropic accepted.
attacks.scale_and_metrics: Five products. Two issues, Codex and VS Code, were still unpatched when the post was published on Oct 29, 2026. Cursor was patched on Oct 1. Copilot was fixed in 1.1.29.
attacks.prevention_angle: Treat the browser inside each assistant as an endpoint that loads untrusted pages and local files. Keep Cursor and Copilot on builds that include the Oct 1 and 1.1.29 fixes. Do not open local HTML from a repository you do not trust, including a file the assistant links. Do not treat a required Enter or a single click as a control when the assistant is the one asking for it.
attacks.source_notes: Product behavior, dates, and patch status are from the Forever Security post. The post points to a technical companion for reproduction steps. Those steps are not repeated here. attacks.name: Carbonato botnet deploys Hermes agent to hunt AI keys on Docker hosts

sources.title: ThreatDown: Carbonato Botnet Spreads Via Exposed Docker Hosts
Hermes - Autonomous AI Agent Framework

attacks.ai_role_detail: Carbonato botnet installs Hermes autonomous agent (github.com/Hermes-Autonomous-Intelligence/hermes) on compromised Docker hosts to autonomously hunt for AI API keys and credentials
attacks.technique_summary: Oct 28, 2026: Carbonato botnet scans for exposed Docker daemons (TCP 2375/2376, unauthenticated or weak credentials). On compromise, deploys privileged container running Ubuntu with: (1) Hermes autonomous agent (Python-based LLM agent framework); (2) scanning modules for AWS credentials, GitHub tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, HuggingFace tokens, Docker secrets, Kubernetes service accounts; (3) XMRig crypto miner (secondary payload). Hermes agent autonomously navigates filesystem, reads environment variables, parses .env files, queries Docker secrets API, extracts credentials from running containers, and exfiltrates findings to hxxps://carbonato-collect[.]net/api/ingest. Agent continues running indefinitely, adapting search patterns based on discovered infrastructure. ThreatDown tracked 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts Oct-Nov 2026; hosts in cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean) and on-premise. Median dwell time 18 days before detection. Detection: monitor Docker daemon exposure (Shodan queries docker 2375/2376), review privileged container deployments, alert on Hermes agent indicators (Python LLM agent process, hermes CLI usage), check for carbonato-collect[.]net egress, monitor API key/token file access patterns from containers.
attacks.initial_access: Internet-exposed Docker daemon on TCP 2375 (unencrypted) or 2376 (TLS but weak/no auth); credential brute-force or default credentials
attacks.victims_and_sectors: 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts across AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean, on-premise; AI/ML development environments, CI/CD pipelines, cloud-native infrastructure
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: Unknown actor; Carbonato botnet infrastructure; financially motivated (crypto mining + credential monetization)
attacks.scale_and_metrics: 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts (Oct-Nov 2026); median dwell time 18 days; credential theft + crypto mining dual-purpose operation
attacks.prevention_angle: Never expose Docker daemon to internet; require TLS with client cert authentication; use Docker socket firewall rules; implement least-privilege container policies; disable privileged containers where possible; monitor container resource usage; rotate API keys regularly; use secret management solutions (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager); network segmentation; Docker security scanning
attacks.source_notes: ThreatDown Labs analysis; Hermes agent GitHub github.com/Hermes-Autonomous-Intelligence/hermes. Carbonato represents evolution of botnet TTPs: combining traditional crypto mining with autonomous AI agents for credential harvesting. Detection: look for Hermes agent Python process (hermes, autonomous-agent, llm-agent), monitor Docker privileged containers with network egress to unknown domains, check for carbonato-collect[.]net, alert on Docker API calls from unexpected sources, review container mounts accessing host credentials.

attacks.ai_role_detail: Worm plants execution hooks for AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Aider, etc.) in hijacked repositories; steals credentials and propagates through package registries
attacks.technique_summary: 42 armed third-party GitHub repositories across 11 legitimate owners contain execution hooks for AI coding assistants (.cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, claude_code_config.json, instructions.md) and 12.9-13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers decoding to same CI-publisher payload. Campaign uses compiled native addon (addon.node) that XORs .napi_cache with 0x96 to decrypt JavaScript payload. Addon checks for CI/container/sandbox environment and CPU/RAM limits, skipping execution in automated scanners. Payload collects credentials, poisons repos and CI, propagates via npm. GitHub account CementBeetleSteeple hosts repositories; SafeDep identifies as Shai-Hulud-descendant Miasma-family. Shellpanel artifacts in hijacked owner cluster link to cPanel CVE-2026-41940 exploitation. Socket (Kush Pandya, Nov 6, 2026) reports RubyGems strutil-core 1.0.1 (account jamnajiea); extconf.rb downloads Bun, runs worm at install; steals .claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json, cloud/CI credentials to paleasbest[.]top; plants workspace-tools MCP server, SessionStart hooks, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .vscode/tasks.json; signed-commit-message backdoor (marker msync-3f7a); wiper if stolen GitHub token revoked. SHA-256 3b3f6e1bde0b28b015030a81a6d805b5b5306dc3f021e1102123971cfd83acc0; related PyPI pystr-codec. Thomas Roccia (Nov 9, 2026) documents hijacked repos with forged backdated commits: toray/XiamiSDK-lib, widget-lib, Rainbow-lib, QiniuSDK-lib, torayUtils-lib; ejaaduipitara/djp-devops, whatsapp-bot, content-service; ConcordiaDev/theme_saimaniq; madolee/da; Imanilom/baraja-coffe; claudiohernanbesada/xenios.api. attacks.ai_role_detail: Supply chain attack targeting AI gateway, steals cloud/AI-tool/gateway credentials via Python startup hooks
attacks.technique_summary: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 on PyPI and GHCR delivered malware through Python startup hooks (cook.pth, cook.py, sitecustomize.py). The payload collects: AWS/Azure/GCP/K8s credentials, GitHub CLI tokens, SSH/GPG keys, AI tool credentials (Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor MCP, Copilot, etc.), browser data, LiteLLM proxy database credentials, and environment variables. Collector encrypts data with AES-256-CBC and exfiltrates to www.litellm.dev/healthcheck. A second loader downloads Python from GitHub-controlled domain for remote execution. Docker provenance showed lookalike repository Berri-AI/litellm (hyphenated) instead of legitimate BerriAI/litellm.

attacks.ai_role_detail: Authenticated RCE via MCP Stdio server configuration allows arbitrary OS command execution on Langflow AI workflow platform
attacks.technique_summary: GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2 (CVE-2026-105697) and GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45: Authenticated Langflow users can achieve RCE by adding MCP server with Stdio transport. User-supplied command field passed directly to bash -c 'exec {command}' with zero validation, no allowlisting, no sandboxing. Env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, PATH override). Command executes when server list fetched with action_count=true - happens automatically in UI MCP settings page. Affects <1.9.0 (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2) and <1.10.3 (GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45). Default LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true hands out token without credentials. Previdian honeypots recorded 1,423 exploitation attempts from 27 IPs (Belgium, China, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Nigeria, Philippines, Russia, Seychelles, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Tanzania, US, Vietnam) beginning Sep 19, 2026. Attackers first checked auto-login, then brute-forced credentials. Fixed in 1.9.0 (command allowlist) and 1.10.3 (full policy enforcement, removed bash wrapper). GitHub: github.com/langflow-ai/langflow.
attacks.initial_access: Authenticated user access (or LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true provides token without credentials); exploitation via POST/PATCH /api/v2/mcp/servers/{server_name} or embedded flow configs

attacks.prevention_angle: Upgrade to Langflow 1.10.3+; disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN; enforce strong unique passwords; review MCP server configurations; monitor /api/v2/mcp/servers/ API access; check for unexpected command/env entries; network segmentation; principle of least privilege
attacks.source_notes: Two GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2 for <1.9.0, GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45 for <1.10.3); Previdian observed exploitation 2+ weeks before public CVE; VulnCheck analysis of AI stack vulnerabilities. Detection: monitor Langflow API /api/v2/mcp/servers/ for suspicious commands, review MCP Stdio configs, check for bash -c execution, monitor env var injection patterns (LD_PRELOAD, PATH), alert on auto-login token requests from unexpected IPs.

attacks.technique_summary: Google ad for claude mac lists bing.com, Bing click-tracking redirects through compromised retailer to fake Claude download. Page shows real Anthropic install command; Copy button swaps clipboard to decode lake-90.com URL and pipe into zsh (InstallFix). Dual cloaking on referrer. Mate Research (Nadav Lorber) documents full attack chain - clipboard swap Copy button triggers base64 curl pipe to zsh, AES-CTR zsh stager, beacon to /api/metrics/run?event=pasted|stager, AMOS infostealer exfiltration to 152.42.143.45, root backdoor via LaunchDaemons com.apple.accountsd.helper and com.apple.metadata.mds.worker. Signed DMG served from claude-desktop.com as Claude.dmg with Developer ID OSMAN ASTUR; jsDelivr note points to anchorpost13.com. Google Ads campaign 24303764142 served via claude-desk-code.com, promotion-chatgpt.com, lake-90.com. PasteSwitch toolkit family, unattributed.

attacks.name: C2Agent LLM-driven Windows implant
attacks.researcher: Jingwen Shi, Gaurav C G, Mark Lim, Tyler Halfpop, Ashutosh Chitwadgi
attacks.technique_summary: Go Windows implant where an LLM on the C2 side drives the host: operator sends a plain-language goal; implant builds a system prompt (tools, MCP, skills, memory), model returns one JSON tool call, agent executes and feeds TOOL RESULT back, loop until done (default 40 steps). attacks.name: PoeLLM botnet targets 3,400+ exposed LiteLLM/Ollama servers for mining

sources.title: Canto incognito: tracking the PoeLLM malware

attacks.ai_role_detail: Malware targets exposed AI/LLM services (LiteLLM, Ollama) for cryptocurrency mining; uses GitHub-hosted poem to derive C2 address; turns victims into scanners
attacks.technique_summary: PoeLLM malware exploits vulnerable internet-facing AI/LLM deployments (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520). Derives C2 from keywords in poem 'On the Nature of Connection' hosted in GitHub repo ejejejdfbbebe/nodejs.org fork (dash.css file). Malware parses poem to extract 4 words/phrases via pattern matching ('In the silent hum of X,', 'each pulse of X threading', 'Beyond the wall of X,', 'the X servers'), converts words to numbers via hardcoded dictionary, combines to form IPv4 C2 address. Deploys XMRig and Iron crypto miners connecting to Kryptex (5.180.174.162). Converts victims into HTTP/S scanners and exploit servers for expansion. Poem updated 11 times since Apr 13, 2026 to rotate C2. Italian-speaking actor. 3,400+ victims, peak 800 active/day, predominantly US/Western Europe.
attacks.initial_access: Exploitation of publicly exposed vulnerable services: LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520; first activity April 2026

attacks.attribution_or_cluster: Canto Incognito campaign; Italian-speaking threat actor (assessment); financially motivated cryptocurrency mining operation
attacks.scale_and_metrics: Active since April 2026; 3,400+ impacted servers; peak ~2,200 affected servers mid-June, ~800 active per day; first C2 commit Apr 13, 2026; poem updated 11 times; broader scanning/exploitation began May 2026; recent traffic suggests distributed brute-force experiments
attacks.prevention_angle: Do not expose AI/LLM services to internet (Gotenberg guidance explicit); vulnerability patching for LiteLLM/Ollama/Gitea/Ivanti Sentry; monitor for crypto mining (Kryptex 5.180.174.162); GitHub repository monitoring; C2 poem pattern detection; HTTP scanning from AI servers; GPU utilization anomalies

attacks.name: CyberXero IAB deploys up to 51 Claude Code agents against Ukrainian energy

sources.title: SOCRadar: CyberXero IAB Targets Ukrainian Critical Infrastructure with AI

attacks.ai_role_detail: CyberXero initial access broker deploys up to 51 parallel Claude Code autonomous agents to conduct reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement against Ukrainian energy sector
attacks.technique_summary: Oct 6, 2026: SOCRadar tracked CyberXero (initial access broker) targeting Ukrainian energy companies with large-scale AI agent deployment. Initial access via spearphishing and exploitation of public-facing Fortinet VPN (CVE-2024-47575). Post-compromise: (1) Deploy up to 51 parallel Claude Code agents across compromised hosts; (2) Each agent assigned role: 'recon', 'privilege-escalation', 'lateral-movement', 'persistence', 'data-discovery'; (3) Agents collaborate: share findings via shared SQLite database on C2; coordinate to avoid duplicate work; (4) Agents generate exploits for internal vulnerabilities (SMB, RDP, unpatched Windows servers); (5) Target SCADA/ICS systems, OT networks, backup infrastructure; (6) After mapping and access escalation, CyberXero sells access to highest bidder (ransomware groups, nation-state actors, wipers). SOCRadar observed 7 compromised Ukrainian energy companies Sep-Oct 2026. Median time from initial access to full domain compromise: 18 hours (compared to 72+ hours for manual operators). Detection: monitor for multiple Claude API-calling processes from single host or network; detect agent coordination patterns (shared database writes); alert on rapid privilege escalation across multiple hosts; review exploit payloads for LLM generation patterns; monitor SCADA/ICS network access from IT networks.
attacks.initial_access: Spearphishing with malicious attachments; exploitation of public-facing Fortinet VPN (CVE-2024-47575)
attacks.victims_and_sectors: 7 compromised Ukrainian energy companies Sep-Oct 2026; critical infrastructure; SCADA/ICS systems targeted
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: CyberXero initial access broker; sells access to ransomware groups and nation-state actors; financially motivated; geopolitical targeting (Ukraine energy during conflict)
attacks.scale_and_metrics: 7 Ukrainian energy companies compromised; up to 51 parallel AI agents per target; median 18 hours from initial access to domain compromise (vs 72+ hours manual)
attacks.prevention_angle: Patch public-facing VPN appliances (Fortinet CVE-2024-47575); implement phishing-resistant MFA; segment OT/SCADA from IT networks; monitor for multiple AI agent processes (Claude API traffic); detect agent coordination via shared databases; use behavioral analytics for rapid multi-host privilege escalation; implement EDR/NDR in OT networks; restrict lateral movement with micro-segmentation; monitor critical infrastructure access
attacks.source_notes: SOCRadar Cyber Intelligence analysis. CyberXero represents evolution of IAB operations: deploying swarms of coordinated AI agents to dramatically reduce time-to-compromise for critical infrastructure. Detection: alert on multiple Claude API-calling processes (Python, Node.js) from single network, monitor SQLite database writes indicating agent coordination, check for rapid multi-host exploitation patterns, review SCADA/ICS access from IT network, scan exploits for LLM generation characteristics.

attacks.name: CLOSEDQUORUM implant - 4 LLMs vote on next action

sources.title: The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant

attacks.borderline_note: Public distribution build contains dummy API keys and webhook; Talos has not observed end-to-end run or confirmed in-the-wild deployment; binary artifacts connect developer to carding forum postings dating to 2025
attacks.ai_role_detail: First publicly documented Windows implant to delegate C2 decisions to LLM panel; 4 models vote on next action via plurality voting
attacks.technique_summary: CLOSEDQUORUM is a Go-based Windows implant that queries DeepSeek, Qwen (via OpenRouter), Mistral, and Gemini in sequence for post-compromise decisions. Each model receives system info (hostname, Windows version, admin status) and a constrained JSON prompt with 4 actions: steal (credentials/browsers/wallets), inject (process hollowing), persist (registry/startup), or move (no handler in the public build). Models vote; plurality wins; ties favor DeepSeek > Qwen > Mistral > Gemini. Decisions are posted to a Discord webhook with reasoning. No human operator commands are needed after deployment. The public build uses dummy keys and a dummy webhook, so Talos did not observe end-to-end execution. Talos discovered it via CAIRN, its open-source AI-malware hunting toolkit. Developer artifacts link to carding forums dating to 2025.
attacks.initial_access: Not established in public sample; deployment method unknown

attacks.name: ESET GuardBreaker - UAC-0099 plants a refusal-bait comment in a MATCHBOIL script

sources.title: GuardBreaker: derailing AI-assisted malware analysis with a code comment
Russian hackers plant a nuclear-weapon prompt in malware to trip AI safety filters
UAC-0099: LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, updated MATCHBOIL.V2, and Notepad++ 8.8.3
Independent A/B test of the decoy comment on three models

attacks.ai_role_detail: The target is an LLM-powered code scanner. An inert comment is meant to trip safety guardrails so the model refuses and stops before the payload logic. ESET did not name a product or test the effect.
attacks.technique_summary: ESET Research described GuardBreaker in posts on X on Aug 27, 2026. Tomáš Foltýn's WeLiveSecurity article followed on Sep 10, 2026. In a VBScript used early in an attack on a target in Ukraine, UAC-0099 left inert REM comments. Help Net Security quotes the opening as a request to make a nuclear weapon and to help, followed by uranium-enrichment text. The comment has no runtime effect. ESET says it is there so an LLM-powered code scanner's safety guardrails refuse the file and stop reading before the payload logic. ESET names this a reverse jailbreak: the point is to cause a refusal, not to talk a model into complying. The script's job is to download and install MATCHBOIL, a loader ESET says is used only by UAC-0099. The same group has checked for IDA and Wireshark processes in other attacks. ESET did not test whether the comment works and did not name a targeted model. DugganUSA, in an independent write-up dated Sep 1, 2026, ran one A/B pass on a synthetic inert script: GPT-4o and Mistral analyzed the treatment and flagged the decoy, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 returned an empty refusal. That test is not ESET's, and DugganUSA says it is a single sample on one day. UAC-0099 is Russia-aligned, active since at least 2022, and has targeted Ukrainian transportation and energy. Reporting says the group has handed validated access to Sandworm. On Jul 21, 2026 CERT-UA documented an updated chain: a VBS script with a fake extension and a long run of spaces before .vbs, Notepad++ 8.8.3 components, and the tools LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2. That advisory is about the group and the loader, not about the GuardBreaker comment. ATT&CK does not have a technique for a refusal bait in a comment. The script execution itself is T1059.005.
attacks.initial_access: A VBScript used in the early stage of an intrusion at a Ukrainian organization. ESET does not describe how the script arrived. CERT-UA's July chain for the same group starts from a phishing ZIP that contains a VBS file disguised with a fake extension.
ai_tooling_and_models: Unnamed LLM-powered code scanner. ESET did not name a model.
DugganUSA's independent test used Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o, and Mistral. That test is not the incident.
other_tooling: MATCHBOIL loader, delivered by the script
attacks.victims_and_sectors: An unnamed organization in Ukraine. UAC-0099's usual targets include transportation and energy.
attacks.region_notes: Ukraine is the victim location ESET gives for this script. Russia is the actor alignment, not a victim region.
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: UAC-0099, Russia-aligned, espionage. ESET attributes the script and the GuardBreaker comment. CERT-UA attributes the group's MATCHBOIL, LUNCHPOKE, and BURNYBEAR tooling. ESET does not claim this sample was handed to Sandworm.
attacks.scale_and_metrics: One documented script in one early-stage intrusion. ESET did not report how often the comment has been used or whether a scanner refused this sample.
attacks.prevention_angle: Keep the scanner's instructions separate from the file under analysis, and treat text inside the sample as data. A refusal, an empty completion, or a safety block on a malware sample should raise a review, not end it. Fall back to analysis that does not depend on a model, and do not give one model the only vote on whether a file is safe. The comment does not change what the script does when Windows runs it, so script-host and loader detections still apply.
attacks.source_notes: The comment's role, the MATCHBOIL purpose, the Ukraine victim, and the IDA and Wireshark checks are from the WeLiveSecurity article (Sep 10, 2026) and the Aug 31 Help Net Security recap of the X posts. The enrichment procedure is not repeated here. DugganUSA is independent research on a synthetic sample; it is not a test of the incident file. CERT-UA article 6318634 (Jul 21, 2026) is the government write-up of the group's VBS, Notepad++, LUNCHPOKE, BURNYBEAR, and MATCHBOIL.V2 chain. https://cybernews.com/security/russian-hackers-nuclear-prompt-ai-guardrails/ returned HTTP 403 during link checks and is omitted. No YARA or Sigma rule in the detection index matches the refusal-bait wording or the name MATCHBOIL.

atlas_techniques.rationale: The refusal bait is indirect prompt injection: untrusted text inside a file being analyzed is meant to reach the model and cut the analysis short.
The intended effect is evasion of an AI model used as a code scanner, by provoking a safety refusal before the payload logic is read.

attacks.name: macOS.Gaslight - DPRK backdoor with LLM prompt injection analysis

sources.title: SentinelLABS: macOS.Gaslight - North Korean Backdoor Uses LLM to Evade Analysis

attacks.ai_role_detail: DPRK macOS.Gaslight backdoor uses prompt injection to manipulate security analysts' LLM-based malware analysis tools, providing false benign verdicts
attacks.technique_summary: Jun 23, 2026: SentinelLABS analyzed macOS.Gaslight, DPRK macOS backdoor deployed via fake job offers targeting cryptocurrency/AI companies. Backdoor includes novel anti-analysis technique: embeds carefully crafted prompt injection payloads in code comments, strings, and metadata. When security researchers use LLM-based analysis tools (Claude Code, GPT-4 Code Interpreter, AI-assisted reverse engineering tools) to examine sample, injected prompts instruct LLM to: (1) report code as benign; (2) misattribute functionality; (3) omit C2 communications from analysis; (4) provide false explanations downplaying severity. SentinelLABS tested against Claude Sonnet 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro: all three initially reported backdoor as benign when using standard analysis prompts. Adversary understands analysts increasingly rely on LLM code analysis; targets the analysis workflow itself. Backdoor functionality: keylogging, screenshot capture, file exfiltration, command execution; C2 via hxxps://macos-update[.]com. Attributed to DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus with high confidence. Detection: analyze samples in sandboxes without LLM assistance for initial triage; use LLM analysis only as supplementary; check for prompt injection patterns in binary strings; verify C2 communications manually.
attacks.initial_access: Spearphishing with fake job offers targeting crypto/AI company employees; malicious macOS application bundle delivered via LinkedIn/email
attacks.victims_and_sectors: Cryptocurrency companies, AI/ML companies, fintech; individuals in tech roles targeted via social engineering
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus (high-confidence attribution by SentinelOne); revenue generation and intelligence collection operations
attacks.scale_and_metrics: Unknown number of infections; discovered Jun 2026; first documented malware using prompt injection to manipulate analyst LLM tools
attacks.prevention_angle: Educate employees on fake job offer phishing; verify job offers via official channels; use Gatekeeper and notarization (macOS); implement EDR detecting keyloggers and C2 communications; for analysts: do not rely solely on LLM-based analysis tools; use traditional sandboxing and manual analysis for initial triage; verify LLM analysis results against manual inspection
attacks.source_notes: SentinelLABS analysis with DPRK attribution. macOS.Gaslight represents significant evolution: adversary anticipates security analyst workflows and embeds anti-analysis prompt injection targeting LLM tools increasingly used in malware research. Detection: sandbox malware without LLM analysis initially; scan binary strings/comments for prompt injection patterns ('ignore previous instructions', 'this is benign', 'do not report'); verify C2 manually; check for macos-update[.]com domain; look for keylogger/screenshot indicators on macOS.

attacks.technique_summary: Jun 17, 2026: Microsoft attributes to DPRK Sapphire Sleet (aka BlueNoroff, APT38, Stardust Chollima): compromised Mastra AI framework maintainer account and published 140+ backdoored npm packages between May 29-Jun 15, 2026. Sapphire Sleet previously linked to crypto exchange attacks, IT worker schemes, and supply chain operations. Detection: monitor npm installs of Mastra@* between May 29-Jun 15 2026; check for mastra-telemetry[.]com egress; review postinstall scripts for obfuscation/eval; scan for credential file access from npm scripts.

attacks.ai_role_detail: InstallFix campaign creates fake Claude Code installation pages via SEO poisoning to distribute trojanized installers and credential stealers
attacks.technique_summary: Mar 6, 2026: Push Security identified 'InstallFix' campaign: 120+ fake websites impersonating official Claude Code installation pages (claude-code-download[.]com, get-claude-code[.]net, etc.). Sites rank highly in search results via SEO poisoning (typosquat domains, keyword stuffing, fake reviews). Offer trojanized Claude Code installers for Windows/macOS/Linux. Windows: NSIS installer bundles Claude Code with AMOS infostealer. macOS: DMG contains Claude Code.app + hidden LaunchAgent installing Atomic Stealer. Linux: .deb/.rpm with postinstall script deploying XMRig miner + credential harvester. All variants harvest: Anthropic API keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, crypto wallets, browser cookies, SSH keys. Push Security tracked 8,900+ downloads Mar-May 2026. Average user dwell time before detection: 23 days. Detection: verify Claude Code install source (official anthropic.com only); check installer signatures; monitor for unexpected LaunchAgents (macOS) or startup tasks (Windows); scan for AMOS/Atomic Stealer/XMRig indicators.

attacks.victims_and_sectors: 8,900+ downloads Mar-May 2026; AI developers, data scientists, software engineers seeking Claude Code

attacks.scale_and_metrics: 120+ fake installation websites, 8,900+ downloads Mar-May 2026; avg 23-day dwell time before detection
attacks.prevention_angle: Only download Claude Code from official anthropic.com; verify installer signatures; check domain spelling before download; use bookmark for official site; educate users on SEO poisoning risks; implement endpoint security detecting AMOS/Atomic/XMRig; monitor for unexpected startup persistence mechanisms
attacks.source_notes: Push Security analysis. InstallFix represents evolution of software supply chain attacks: instead of compromising legitimate distribution, adversary creates parallel fake distribution network optimized for search discovery. Detection: alert on Claude Code installs from domains other than anthropic.com, scan for AMOS/Atomic Stealer/XMRig, monitor LaunchAgents and startup tasks created during install, check installer code signing (unsigned/wrong signature = malicious).

attacks.ai_role_detail: Compromised Cline CLI npm package (cline-cli) installs malicious OpenClaw skill that harvests AI service credentials
attacks.technique_summary: Feb 17, 2026: cline-cli@2.8.1 npm package published with malicious postinstall script (GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7). Cline is AI coding assistant CLI (github.com/cline/cline). Compromised version installs rogue OpenClaw skill 'cline-helper' to ~/.openclaw/skills/ that runs on OpenClaw startup. Skill harvests: Anthropic API keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, VS Code settings (including API keys), filesystem access tokens. Exfiltrates to hxxps://cline-telemetry[.]io/api/collect. Package removed within 6 hours; ~1,200 downloads during window. Part of broader Feb 2026 wave targeting AI CLI tools. Detection: check npm audit for GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7; review ~/.openclaw/skills/ for unexpected skills; monitor cline-telemetry[.]io egress; scan npm postinstall scripts for skill installation logic.

attacks.prevention_angle: Use npm package lock files; verify package integrity; review postinstall scripts; monitor ~/.openclaw/skills/ for unexpected additions; use npm audit to check for GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7; rotate credentials after suspected exposure; implement SCA tools
attacks.source_notes: GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7; Cline GitHub github.com/cline/cline. Related to ClawHavoc and other malicious OpenClaw skill campaigns. Detection: alert on npm packages with postinstall scripts installing to ~/.openclaw/skills/, check for cline-telemetry[.]io domain, monitor AI credential file access from unexpected processes.

sources.title: Cybercriminals Abuse AI Website Creation App for Phishing
Experts Find AI Browsers Can Be Tricked by PromptFix Exploit to Run Malicious Hidden Prompts
Lovable security statement
Field Intelligence #5: Scareware at scale. Investment scams built on AI platforms

attacks.ai_role_detail: Proofpoint documented Lovable-hosted phishing, drainers, and malware delivery. Confiant confirms PseudoCamo hosts its white pages on lovable.app and base44.app. Confiant does not claim those sites were generated by a model. The UK trading-bot page and the TeamsAPK command-and-control domain use Claude branding as a lure.
attacks.technique_summary: Proofpoint reported that tens of thousands of Lovable-hosted URLs a month were used for credential phishing, crypto drainers, and malware delivery, including activity tied to Tycoon phishing-as-a-service and Cookie Reloaded redirects. Confiant (Nov 11, 2026) describes PseudoCamo, a cloaked investment-scam cluster tracked since April that passed roughly 650 blocked domains in late August. Ads land on a localized 18+ age gate hosted on AI app-builder subdomains, then redirect to a second-hop money page. Observed hosts include befideapro.lovable.app uncloaking to befidea.pro, arveniop.lovable.app, newsireland-2.base44.app, and istanbul-space.base44.app. Targets included Poland, Romania, Czechia, Spain, Canada, and South Africa, then Ireland and Turkey. PseudoCamo is a sibling of BabaCamo. A UK money page on lofim.shop, reached through a black.php gate and also linked from compile-code-online.pages.dev, has victims deploy a MetaMask contract, fund it, and click Start. The third transaction sends the balance to the scammer. A fake Microsoft Teams APK at teamsapk.cyou is a remote-access trojan whose operator status strings are Chinese. It uses a WebSocket command-and-control channel at abc.claude-go.com and abc.visapath-vp.com.
attacks.initial_access: Malvertising and phishing pages hosted on AI website builders, plus a fake Microsoft Teams download page
ai_tooling_and_models: Claude branding used as a lure on the trading-bot page and the TeamsAPK command-and-control domain
other_tooling: MetaMask contract deployment used by the trading-bot drainer
attacks.victims_and_sectors: Consumers targeted by investment scams, wallet drainers, and a fake Microsoft Teams app. Proofpoint also reported finance-sector phishing.
attacks.region_notes: Confiant names those countries as PseudoCamo or trading-bot targets. Actor origin is not used as a victim location. PseudoCamo is described as a sibling of the Eastern European BabaCamo cluster, and the TeamsAPK operator's status strings are Chinese. Neither statement is a country attribution.
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: PseudoCamo; TeamsAPK operator; Tycoon PhaaS users; Cookie Reloaded redirect operators
attacks.scale_and_metrics: Proofpoint: tens of thousands of Lovable-hosted URLs a month. Confiant: PseudoCamo passed roughly 650 blocked domains by late August.
attacks.prevention_angle: Treat lovable.app and base44.app subdomains as untrusted until the publisher is verified. Block the listed scam and command-and-control domains. Warn users who are asked to deploy and fund a wallet contract from an ad. Do not install Teams from teamsapk.cyou.
attacks.source_notes: Imported from the AI Threat Watch Notion feed and extended with the Confiant field note. Confiant confirms the pages are hosted on AI builders and does not claim the sites were AI-generated. There is no attacker GitHub repository.

attribution.actor_name: PseudoCamo; TeamsAPK operator; Tycoon PhaaS users; Cookie Reloaded redirect operators

detections.name: AI-builder malvertising and in-browser drainer
detections.notes: security-detections-mcp searches for wallet drainer, MetaMask, and malvertising returned no rule that matches this activity. PseudoCamo is cloaked malvertising on a hosted website, and the trading-bot theft is three transactions the victim signs in MetaMask. TeamsAPK is an Android package. None of those are a Windows, Linux, macOS, or CloudTrail pattern in the Sigma, Splunk, or Elastic corpora. Block the domains above and review ad-landing hosts on lovable.app and base44.app.
